# Compare gene structure, alignment, and RNA-seq

Compare the Dox locus in *Drosophila mauritiana*, *D. simulans*, and
*D. sechellia*. Each window contains the flanking genes `CG42797` and
`Ptpmeg2`; *D. simulans* also contains a `Dox` coding model. The locus comes
from [Extended Data Figure 5 of Vedanayagam et al.
(2021)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8665063/#F11).

Prepare one `SynSpecies` containing the three assemblies, their feature and
RNA-seq annotations, and two pairwise alignments. Then draw the gene models,
add nucleotide links, and place one combined RNA-seq track above each species.
All plotting inputs are bundled and work offline.
See the [data README](https://github.com/DongyaoLiu/ggexon/blob/HEAD/inst/extdata/dox_synteny/README.md#data-provenance-and-interpretation)
for detailed provenance, model reconstruction, and remapping checks.

# Present the inputs

The annotation models and alignments describe the selected chromosome-X
windows. RNA-seq comes from **testis biological replicate 1** in
[GEO series GSE185361](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE185361):

| Species | RNA-seq sample | Signal used here |
|:--|:--|:--|
| *D. mauritiana* | [GSM5611558](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSM5611558) | Deposited forward and reverse BigWigs |
| *D. simulans* | [GSM7039340](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSM7039340) | Original paired-end reads, [SRR23418969](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/browser/view/SRR23418969), remapped to the plotted assembly |
| *D. sechellia* | [GSM5611560](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSM5611560) | Deposited forward and reverse BigWigs |

The deposited *D. simulans* BigWigs use a different assembly, so the bundle
uses coverage recomputed from the complete original read library on
**GCA_004382185.1**. The other two species retain deposited signal values.
These units differ: use the tracks to compare signal position and shape;
cross-species peak heights do not measure relative expression abundance.

For this tutorial, strand separation is unnecessary. Preparation combines
the two source tracks **at each genomic base**:

```text
combined signal = abs(forward signal) + abs(reverse signal)
```

The reverse source scores use a negative sign to identify strand. Summing
the magnitudes prevents cancellation where both strands have signal.
Preparation retains genomic positions and applies no smoothing or additional
normalization. Each species has one `.RNA.bw` file. The original strand
files remain available for the separate-strand example in Basic usage.

Locate the installed files and inspect their assembly windows:

```{r dox-inputs}
library(ggexon)
library(ggplot2)

demo_dir <- system.file("extdata", "dox_synteny", package = "ggexon")
stopifnot(nzchar(demo_dir))
object_dir <- file.path(demo_dir, "objects")
windows <- read.delim(file.path(demo_dir, "windows.tsv"))
species_ids <- windows$species

knitr::kable(windows[, c("name", "accession", "chrom", "start", "end", "sample")],
  row.names = FALSE)
```

| Files in `objects/` | Contents | Object used below |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `Dmau.gtf`, `Dsim.gtf`, `Dsech.gtf` | Gene/transcript spans and disjoint CDS/UTR pieces | `SynIndividual`, with a feature annotation |
| `Dmau_Dsim.paf`, `Dsim_Dsech.paf` | Ungapped LASTZ alignment blocks | `SynPairAlignment` |
| `Dmau.RNA.bw`, `Dsim.RNA.bw`, `Dsech.RNA.bw` | Combined RNA-seq signal | `SynBigWigAnnotation` |

All plotting files use `X` as a chromosome-name alias and retain coordinates
on the listed assemblies. GTF and queried feature intervals are one-based
and inclusive. Raw PAF starts are zero-based; the ggexon importer converts
them once. Do not subtract one again after import.

The GTFs are curated display models derived from source annotations.
CDS and UTR pieces do not overlap. The Dox model contains three coding exons;
its UTRs and CDS phase were not reconstructed. A full genome FASTA is not
needed to draw these imported features.

The BigWig backend requires macOS or Linux. The annotation and alignment
plots can also be followed on Windows.

# Prepare the comparative Syn object

## Attach the feature and RNA-seq annotations

A `SynIndividual` stores one assembly's annotation layers. Its constructor
attaches the GTF as the default feature annotation. Add the combined BigWig
as a named `RNA_seq` annotation, then collect the three individuals in one
`SynSpecies`. Keep the assembly accession, sample ID, and signal units with
the data:

```{r dox-annotation-objects}
comparison <- SynSpecies(name = "Dox insertion locus")
for (id in species_ids) {
  w <- windows[windows$species == id, ]
  individual <- SynIndividual(
    id = id,
    annotation_file = file.path(object_dir, paste0(id, ".gtf")),
    annotation_format = "gtf",
    metadata = list(assembly = w$accession, original_contig = w$chrom)
  )
  signal_unit <- if (id == "Dsim") "primary read depth" else "deposited signal"
  individual <- add_annotation(individual, SynBigWigAnnotation(
    name = "RNA_seq",
    bigwig_file = file.path(object_dir, paste0(id, ".RNA.bw")),
    metadata = list(sample = w$sample, signal_unit = signal_unit,
      score_handling = "sum of forward and reverse signal magnitudes")
  ))
  comparison <- add_individual(comparison, individual)
}
individual_names(comparison)
names(comparison@individuals[["Dsim"]]@annotations)
```

The object now owns the gene models and RNA-seq files. Plotting layers can
select them by individual ID and annotation name; no separate coverage table
is needed for plotting. Attaching a BigWig records its location; regional
queries read the signal when needed.

## Attach the two pairwise alignments

An alignment belongs to the collection because it connects two individuals.
In these PAF files the upper species is the target and the lower species is
the query. Use the same IDs as in the individual constructors:

```{r dox-alignment-objects}
comparison <- add_pairwise_alignment(comparison,
  SynPairAlignment(name = "Dmau_Dsim", target_individual = "Dmau",
    query_individual = "Dsim", file = file.path(object_dir, "Dmau_Dsim.paf"),
    format = "paf"))
comparison <- add_pairwise_alignment(comparison,
  SynPairAlignment(name = "Dsim_Dsech", target_individual = "Dsim",
    query_individual = "Dsech", file = file.path(object_dir, "Dsim_Dsech.paf"),
    format = "paf"))
blocks <- pairwise_alignment_data(comparison, alignment = "Dmau_Dsim")
head(blocks[, c("tchr", "tstart", "tend", "qchr", "qstart", "qend", "nmatch", "alen")])
```

The files contain 41 Dmau-Dsim blocks and 98 Dsim-Dsech blocks. LASTZ generated
the ungapped, chained alignments; retained blocks are at least 80 bp long and
at least 85% identical. No block is removed because it overlaps Dox.

## Store the panel order and genomic windows

Store the complete eight-row layout before plotting: RNA-seq above each
annotation, with a link row between neighboring species. Coverage and
annotation rows share a `track` name; `panel_type` distinguishes their roles.
Each pair shares its assembly's genomic window. Keep the left display margins,
and set the right edge to **9.44 Mb** for Dmau and Dsech. The source windows
in `windows.tsv` remain the original extraction ranges; Dmau's added right-edge
space extends beyond its bundled data.

```{r dox-rna-layout}
window_limits <- setNames(lapply(seq_len(nrow(windows)), function(i)
  c(windows$start[i] - 1L, windows$end[i] + 1L)), species_ids)
for (id in c("Dmau", "Dsech")) window_limits[[id]][2] <- 9440000L

panels <- data.frame(
  PANEL = 1:8, ROW = 1:8, COL = 1L,
  track = c("Dmau", "Dmau", "link_Dmau_Dsim", "Dsim", "Dsim",
    "link_Dsim_Dsech", "Dsech", "Dsech"),
  panel_type = c("coverage", "annotation", "link", "coverage", "annotation",
    "link", "coverage", "annotation"),
  tspecies = c(NA, NA, "Dmau", NA, NA, "Dsim", NA, NA),
  qspecies = c(NA, NA, "Dsim", NA, NA, "Dsech", NA, NA)
)
wi <- match(panels$track, windows$species)
panels$species <- windows$species[wi]
panels$xlim_chr <- ifelse(is.na(wi), NA_character_, "X")
panels$xlim_min <- vapply(window_limits, function(x) x[1], numeric(1))[wi]
panels$xlim_max <- vapply(window_limits, function(x) x[2], numeric(1))[wi]
species_layout(comparison) <- SynLayout(panels = panels,
  free = list(x = TRUE, y = FALSE))
panels[, c("ROW", "track", "panel_type")]
```

Prepare two views for the earlier plotting stages. They retain the same
individuals, annotations, and alignments; only their panel layouts differ:

```{r dox-annotation-views}
annotation_view <- comparison
annotation_panels <- panels[panels$panel_type == "annotation", ]
annotation_panels$PANEL <- annotation_panels$ROW <- seq_len(nrow(annotation_panels))
species_layout(annotation_view) <- SynLayout(panels = annotation_panels,
  free = list(x = TRUE, y = FALSE))

link_view <- comparison
linked_panels <- panels[panels$panel_type != "coverage", ]
linked_panels$PANEL <- linked_panels$ROW <- seq_len(nrow(linked_panels))
species_layout(link_view) <- SynLayout(panels = linked_panels,
  free = list(x = TRUE, y = FALSE))
```

## Inspect the annotations and combined signal

Query gene records and combined RNA-seq from the prepared object. Use the
same y range for all three RNA panels, from zero to `1.1 * max(peaks)`.
This leaves space above the largest signal without rescaling any scores:

```{r dox-inspect-genes}
dsim_genes <- query_features(comparison@individuals[["Dsim"]],
  chr = "X", feature_type = "gene", all = TRUE)
as.data.frame(dsim_genes)[, c("seqnames", "start", "end", "strand", "gene_name")]
```

```{r dox-rna-limits, eval=.Platform$OS.type != "windows"}
peaks <- setNames(vapply(species_ids, function(id) {
  individual <- comparison@individuals[[id]]
  w <- windows[windows$species == id, ]
  signal <- query_signal(get_annotation(individual, "RNA_seq"), "X", w$start, w$end)
  max(S4Vectors::mcols(signal)$score)
}, numeric(1)), species_ids)
rna_limits <- c(0, 1.1 * max(peaks))
knitr::kable(data.frame(species = species_ids, peak = unname(peaks),
  unit = c("deposited signal", "primary read depth", "deposited signal")),
  row.names = FALSE)
```

# Choose the geoms, scales, facet, and theme

## Define the common plotting settings

Use blue for the two flanking genes, orange for Dox, and one blue RNA-seq
fill. Ribbon colours show nucleotide identity. `scales = "free_x"` keeps
each species' genomic axis independent; the RNA panels share one y scale.
Keep genomic spacing with `intron_factor = 1`.

```{r dox-common-style}
palette <- c(
  "CG42797" = "#246589", "Ptpmeg2" = "#246589", "Dox" = "#D55E00",
  "RNA-seq" = "#749CB5",
  "85-95%" = "#E2E7ED", "95-98%" = "#A4BCD0", "98-100%" = "#497D9F"
)
chromosomes <- setNames(rep("X", length(species_ids)), species_ids)
strip_labels <- c(Dmau = "D. mauritiana", Dsim = "D. simulans",
  Dsech = "D. sechellia", link_Dmau_Dsim = "", link_Dsim_Dsech = "")
text_size <- 9 / (72.27 / 25.4)  # ggplot2 geom text sizes use millimeters.

plot_style <- list(
  facet_genomics(vars(track), ncol = 1, scales = "free_x",
    strip.position = "left", strip_group = "individual",
    labeller = as_labeller(strip_labels),
    xlim = window_limits, xlim_chr = chromosomes,
    link_panel_height = 0.5, coverage_panel_height = 0.5,
    link_axis = "none", link_strip = "blank", annotation_axis = "all"),
  scale_panel_annotation("fixed_y"),
  center_panel_annotation(),
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette,
    breaks = c("RNA-seq", "85-95%", "95-98%", "98-100%"),
    labels = c("RNA-seq (combined, ×1)",
      "DNA 85-95%", "DNA 95-98%", "DNA 98-100%"), name = NULL),
  scale_colour_manual(values = palette, guide = "none"),
  scale_x_continuous(oob = scales::oob_keep, expand = expansion(mult = 0)),
  scale_x_ggexon_genomic(intron_factor = 1, n.breaks = 4,
    labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-6, suffix = " Mb", accuracy = 0.01)),
  theme_ggexon_track(base_size = 9, show_x_axis = TRUE,
    show_y_axis = FALSE, show_x_grid = FALSE, show_legend = TRUE),
  theme_ggexon_side_strips("left", base_size = 9, face = "italic"),
  theme(strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, face = "italic"),
    strip.background = element_blank(), panel.border = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = grid::unit(4, "mm"),
    panel.spacing.y = grid::unit(0.3, "lines"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(8, 12, 8, 8)),
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
)
```

Annotation rows have relative height **1**; link and RNA rows each have
height **0.5**. These settings allocate panel space. The shared RNA y limits
above control the signal range within that space.
`oob_keep` retains intervals crossing a display boundary so they are clipped
at the panel edge rather than dropped. Zero x expansion keeps the plotted
axis edges at the requested window limits.

`center_panel_annotation()` centres the gene bodies vertically in their own
panels. `free_x` controls horizontal scales; it does not centre annotations.
Avoid manual annotation y limits here, because named limits take precedence
over centring. `theme_ggexon_side_strips()` puts the species names outside
the axes. With `strip_group = "individual"`, each name spans that individual's
RNA-seq and annotation panels, including their unequal physical heights.

## Draw the gene models

Both annotation layers inherit their data from the Syn object.
`geom_exon2(annotation_type = "all")` draws thick CDS and thinner UTR pieces.
The half-base offsets place rectangle edges around inclusive base positions.
`geom_genelabel()` reads the gene records and adds italic names:

```{r dox-annotation-layers}
annotation_layers <- list(
  geom_exon2(
    aes(fill = gene_name, colour = gene_name, ymin = 1,
      xmin = xmin - 0.5, xmax = xmax + 0.5),
    annotation_type = "all", exon_height = 0.48,
    compress_introns = FALSE, utr_height = 0.45, cds_height = 1,
    intron_shape = "chevron", intron_peak = 0.22, arrow_width = 80,
    linewidth = 0.1, show.legend = FALSE),
  geom_genelabel(aes(colour = gene_name, ymin = 1),
    force_flat = TRUE, exon_height = 0.48, label_offset_fraction = 1.2,
    show_link = FALSE, size = text_size, fontface = "italic", show.legend = FALSE)
)
```

```{r dox-annotation-only, fig.height=3.4, fig.alt="Annotation-only stage: three species with two conserved flanking genes and an orange Dox coding model in D. simulans."}
p_annotation <- ggexon(annotation_view) + annotation_layers + plot_style
p_annotation
```

The blue models show the two conserved flanks; the orange model shows the
additional Dox coding locus in *D. simulans*. Terminal arrows indicate strand.
Genomic distances are retained because intron compression is disabled.

## Add nucleotide links

Select each stored alignment by name. `geom_nuclink()` resolves its species,
chromosomes, and interval endpoints from the object. Fill encodes
`100 * nmatch / alen`, the percentage of matching bases in an ungapped block:

```{r dox-link-layers}
identity_breaks <- c(85, 95, 98, 100)
identity_labels <- c("85-95%", "95-98%", "98-100%")
link_layers <- list(
  geom_nuclink(alignment = "Dmau_Dsim",
    aes(fill = cut(100 * nmatch / alen, breaks = identity_breaks,
      include.lowest = TRUE, labels = identity_labels)),
    alpha = 0.55, colour = NA),
  geom_nuclink(alignment = "Dsim_Dsech",
    aes(fill = cut(100 * nmatch / alen, breaks = identity_breaks,
      include.lowest = TRUE, labels = identity_labels)),
    alpha = 0.55, colour = NA)
)
```

Use the prepared five-panel view and reuse the annotation layers and style:

```{r dox-with-links, fig.height=4.6, fig.alt="Annotation and linkage stage: two nucleotide-link panels connect the three species, each at half the annotation-panel height."}
p_links <- ggexon(link_view) + annotation_layers + link_layers + plot_style
p_links
```

Each ribbon connects intervals on the two neighboring genomic axes. The link
panel has no independent genomic axis. These are sequence-alignment spans;
they do not assign gene orthology. The additional Dsim sequence around Dox
interrupts the otherwise conserved local structure.

## Add one combined RNA-seq track per species

Use the complete `comparison` object and select its `RNA_seq` annotation.
One `geom_coverage()` call reads the three attached BigWigs. The stored layout
places each signal above its own gene models, sharing that individual's
genomic x scale. `scale_panel_coverage("fixed_y")` gives all three RNA panels
one quantitative y scale. The legend marks the signal as **×1**: no region
or track receives a height multiplier.

```{r dox-rna-layers, eval=.Platform$OS.type != "windows"}
rna_layers <- list(
  geom_coverage(aes(fill = "RNA-seq"), annotation = "RNA_seq", alpha = 0.85)
)
p_rna <- ggexon(comparison) +
  annotation_layers +
  link_layers +
  rna_layers +
  plot_style +
  scale_panel_coverage("fixed_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "RNA-seq signal", position = "right",
    breaks = scales::breaks_width(100),
    guide = guide_axis(check.overlap = TRUE),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(), axis.ticks.y = element_line())
```

```{r dox-with-rna, eval=.Platform$OS.type != "windows", fig.cap="The figure combines UCSC GenArk flank annotations and testis RNA-seq from [GSE185361](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE185361) with an orange, three-exon Dox coding model in D. simulans reconstructed from the 474-nt CDS published by [Vedanayagam et al. (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41559-021-01592-z).", fig.alt="Three species with one combined testis RNA-seq track above each centred gene annotation. RNA y axes appear on the right. Each species name is centred outside the left edge of its combined RNA and gene panels. Two nucleotide-link panels connect the species, and Dox is orange in D. simulans."}
p_rna
```

The complete figure has three RNA panels, three annotation panels, and two
link panels. Equal RNA heights now represent equal numeric signal values;
the lower Dsech peak remains lower on the shared axis. Read the signal units
in the table above: deposited scores and remapped read depths remain different
measurements. A peak near Dox locates transcriptional signal; the combined
track does not identify its transcript strand.

`position = "right"` places the RNA y axes on the right. The upper 10%
expansion supplies the range recorded in `rna_limits`, without imposing
RNA-sized y limits on the annotation panels. Gene-panel y positions only
arrange the models and labels; the centring helper keeps the bodies at the
vertical midpoint of each panel.

# Adjust panel heights or compress genomic gaps

To make the linkage or RNA rows smaller, replace the facet with different
physical heights. Reuse the other facet settings so the genomic windows and
strip labels remain the same.

```{r dox-height-controls, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
p_rna + facet_genomics(vars(track), ncol = 1, scales = "free_x",
  strip.position = "left", strip_group = "individual",
  labeller = as_labeller(strip_labels),
  xlim = window_limits, xlim_chr = chromosomes,
  link_panel_height = 0.3, coverage_panel_height = 0.4,
  link_axis = "none", link_strip = "blank", annotation_axis = "all")
```

A number is a height relative to an annotation row. A grid unit such as
`grid::unit(8, "mm")` sets an absolute height instead. `coverage_panel_height`
controls panel size; `scale_panel_coverage()` controls its y range. Changing
one does not require changing the other.

The following scale compresses non-exonic gaps three-fold while retaining
exon widths. It applies the same piecewise map to gene models, RNA intervals,
and both ends of every link. Tick labels remain original genomic coordinates.

```{r dox-compressed, eval=.Platform$OS.type != "windows", fig.cap="The figure combines UCSC GenArk flank annotations and testis RNA-seq from [GSE185361](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE185361) with an orange, three-exon Dox coding model in D. simulans reconstructed from the 474-nt CDS published by [Vedanayagam et al. (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41559-021-01592-z).", fig.alt="The complete object-based figure with gaps compressed three-fold; RNA signals and nucleotide links remain aligned with exon models."}
p_compressed <- p_rna + scale_x_ggexon_genomic(intron_factor = 3,
  n.breaks = 4,
  labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-6, suffix = " Mb", accuracy = 0.01))
p_compressed
```

Gaps include intergenic sequence as well as introns. The compressed view has
no single uniform base-pair scale. Keep genomic coordinates in the objects;
do not compress annotation, signal, or alignment coordinates before plotting.

# Export the plots

Keep `p_annotation`, `p_links`, and `p_rna` as separate objects so you can
export each stage or reuse it in a presentation. These commands write to your
chosen working directory, not into the installed package.

```{r dox-export, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
ggsave("dox-annotation.pdf", p_annotation, width = 9.5, height = 3.4,
  units = "in", device = grDevices::cairo_pdf, bg = "white")
ggsave("dox-with-links.pdf", p_links, width = 9.5, height = 4.6,
  units = "in", device = grDevices::cairo_pdf, bg = "white")
ggsave("dox-with-rna.pdf", p_rna, width = 9.5, height = 6.5,
  units = "in", device = grDevices::cairo_pdf, bg = "white")
ggsave("dox-with-rna.png", p_rna, width = 9.5, height = 6.5,
  units = "in", dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```
